claims.text: The feedstock is gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder.
Rapid melting and solidification during laser powder-bed fusion can produce fine microstructures and improve mechanical properties in high-entropy alloys.
Rapid solidification in conventional laser powder-bed fusion can generate large temperature gradients, residual stresses, and cracks.
The proposed intervention maintains the substrate at approximately -100 °C during laser powder-bed fusion.
A machine-learning model continuously adjusts cooling rate and laser power using real-time temperature-profile feedback.
The proposed processing window uses sub-centimeter features and laser power near 250 W.
Cryogenic substrate pre-cooling suppresses steep thermal gradients during laser powder-bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi.
Reduced thermal gradients promote more uniform solidification and microstructure development.
More uniform solidification limits columnar grain growth.
Reducing thermal gradients minimizes the accumulation of residual stress.
Cryogenic pre-cooling increases heat extraction from the melt pool, lowers peak temperatures, and moderates thermal gradients.
Controlled cooling fosters homogeneous nucleation and growth during solidification.
Machine-learning control of laser energy and cooling produces a more uniform microstructure, reduces defects, and enhances mechanical integrity.
Cryogenically pre-cooled AlCrFeNiSi parts will have statistically significantly lower residual stress than room-temperature-substrate controls.
Cryogenically pre-cooled parts will have a more uniform, fine-grained microstructure than conventional controls.
Cryogenically pre-cooled parts will have higher tensile strength and ductility than conventional controls.
Cryogenic treatments have been shown to mitigate residual stresses in similar high-entropy alloys.

contradictions.description: The intervention and conditions allow continuous machine-learning adjustment of laser power and cooling, but the falsification design says all parameters other than substrate pre-cooling are held constant. Thus the experiment cannot simultaneously test an ML-optimized treatment and isolate pre-cooling as the sole changed variable.
